goal: `mc deploy` and the merge rounds no longer wait for each other. A deploy holds the repository lease only for the seconds it takes to fast-forward `main` and read the sha that ships; the build and `npm run deploy` run on that fixed sha with the lease released, so a gate or merge round can land the next pull request while production is being built, and a deploy can start while a round is measuring. What a deploy ships is still exactly one sha, recorded before the spawn and verified live after it.
contract: Martin, 2026-10-07: a deploy must be able to run at the same time as merges. The lease's one purpose for a deploy — that `main` in `~/memoro` does not move between the question and the read of the sha that ships — is kept; everything after that read runs on the sha, not on `main`.

A deploy still asks its one question, still refuses without a terminal, and still writes its row to `~/mc/runner/log/deploys.tsv` before the spawn and completes it after; `--dry-run` still takes no lease.

A merge round never fast-forwards or otherwise touches the checkout a deploy is building in. Today a deploy builds in the worktree that is `main` (`deploy.js:634`, `source.worktree`); that stays, and the merge round's own writes stay on its candidate worktrees and the forge.
out_of_scope: The gate lock (`gate-lock.js`): one gate round per machine stays as it is; a deploy never took it and still does not.
Any change to `npm run deploy` in memoro, including the pending-migrations preflight it runs.

success_criteria.criterion: While `npm run deploy` is running under `mc deploy`, a `mc merge <repo> <pr>` round claims the repository lease and runs; while a merge round holds the lease, `mc deploy` waits for the fast-forward window rather than refusing, and ships the sha `main` stood on when it got its turn.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/commands/deploy.test.js`: a deploy whose spawn is held open releases the lease before the spawn starts (the fake spawn reads `readLease(PATH)` and sees it free); a deploy started against a held lease with a spawn that releases it a moment later goes through and records the sha read after the fast-forward; `tests/mc/repo-merge.test.js`: a merge round against a lease whose errand begins `deploy ` is not refused when the lease is gone by its claim.

success_criteria.criterion: The help text, the deploy row on the page and the refusal wording say what the lease now covers, and the deploy record is unchanged in shape.
success_criteria.check: `src/mc/help-text.js` § `mc deploy` no longer says the lease is held for the whole deploy; `tests/mc/deploys.test.js` green unchanged; `mc deploy --dry-run --json` output unchanged.

documents.label: merge-robustness, the sibling plan on the same seam

steps.title: The deploy's lease covers the fast-forward and the read of the sha, and nothing after
steps.done_when: In `src/mc/commands/deploy.js` the lease is claimed before `closeAbandoned` and the fast-forward and released right after `shipping` is read and `recordStart` has written its row, before `spawnDeploy`; the `finally` release becomes a guard that only releases a lease this process still holds; `tests/mc/commands/deploy.test.js` pins that the spawn runs with the lease free and that a throw after release does not release somebody else's lease; and the help text and refusal line say so.
instruction: `src/mc/commands/deploy.js:581–664`: the lease is claimed at :583 with errand `deploy <sha>`, `closeAbandoned` runs under it (:594), `main` is fast-forwarded under it (:605–613), `shipping` is read (:619), `recordStart` writes the row (:626), then `spawnDeploy` runs `npm run deploy` in `source.worktree` (:634) and the `finally` at :663 releases. The header comment (:26–29) and the refusal line at :588 say the lease is held for the whole length so `main` cannot move under the build — but the build reads the worktree at the sha it was fast-forwarded to, and a merge landing on `origin/main` afterwards does not move that worktree: nothing fetches or fast-forwards it but this verb (:606) and the person. So the lease is only needed from the claim to the read of `shipping`.

Move the release to right after `recordStart` (so the row carries the sha read under the lease), keep `closeAbandoned` under the lease (it is the deploy-vs-deploy guard: two deploys must still not overlap — see step 2), and turn the `finally` release into `if (stillHeld) release(...)` where `stillHeld` is a flag cleared by the early release — `releaseLease` on a lease another holder has since taken would otherwise hand their repository away (`repo-lease.js`'s own warning about the same thing in `releaseGateLock`'s comment, `gate-lock.js:89–91`). Read `releaseLease` in `src/mc/repo-lease.js` for whether it already refuses to release another holder's lease; if it does, say so in the PR and keep the flag anyway for the message.

Tests in `tests/mc/commands/deploy.test.js`: the suite 'mc deploy — the script under the lease' (:586) pins the lease held during the spawn (`seen[0].lease`) — flip it: the fake spawn reads `readLease(PATH)` and the assertion is that it is free and the row already written. Add: a throw from the spawn after the early release does not release a lease a second holder took in between (claim one in the test with a different holder before the throw). The `--dry-run` test (:234) is unchanged. Update `help-text.js:263–278` ("under mc's lease so nothing moves main while the build reads it" is still true — reword to say the lease covers the read, not the build) and the refusal line at :588 and the header comment.

steps.title: Two deploys still never overlap, and a deploy waits for a merge round's window instead of refusing
steps.done_when: A second `mc deploy` while one is running is refused with the running deploy's sha and start time (from `deploys.tsv`, not from the lease); a `mc deploy` that meets a held lease waits for it the way `mc merge` waits for the gate (`merge-step.js` `WAIT_STOPS`), up to eight minutes, printing who holds it and for what, then takes its window; `tests/mc/commands/deploy.test.js` pins both; the page's deploy section shows a running deploy from the record.
instruction: With step 1 the lease no longer says 'a deploy is running', so the deploy-vs-deploy guard needs its own fact: `lastAttempt` / the `running` rows in `~/mc/runner/log/deploys.tsv` (`src/mc/deploys.js:102–105, 184–197`). A row `running` with no `ended` whose holder pid is alive (read how `lease-liveness.js` decides a pid is alive and reuse it — the row does not carry a pid today, so add a `pid` column the way `closeAbandoned` and the header are versioned: `DEPLOYS_HEADER` and `fileHeader` tolerate an older file) is a deploy in progress: refuse with its sha and start time. A `running` row whose pid is gone is what `closeAbandoned` already marks failed.

The wait: today `claimLease` failing refuses at once (:584–590). Make it wait as `mc merge` does for the gate lock — read `src/mc/merge-step.js` (`WAIT_STOPS`, the eight-minute bound, the 'still waiting' line) and `src/mc/repo-merge.js:163–168`, and reuse the waiting helper rather than writing a second one; print `mc: ~/memoro is held by <holder> for “<errand>” — waiting for the window` and re-claim on the same cadence; after the bound, refuse with exit 3 as the merge does and say to run it again. The `deploys.tsv` row for a refusal keeps saying `refused` with the reason.

Tests: a held lease released by a timer lets the deploy through and the recorded sha is the one read after the fast-forward (fake clock as the merge tests use it); a `running` row with a live pid refuses the second deploy; `src/mc/repo-render.js` `deployRows` (:367) shows the running deploy from the record — read how the page renders a row today before changing it. `help-text.js` gains the waiting sentence.
